articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day Devs 'Proud to Be One of Xbox's Main Titles' Amid Newfound Focus on Exclusivity
articles.summary: The Gears of War: E-Day developers at The Coalition say they are "proud to be one of Xbox's main titles" as Microsoft refocuses on exclusivity.
articles.body:
The Gears of War: E-Day developers at The Coalition say they are "proud to be one of Xbox's main titles" as Microsoft refocuses on exclusivity.

Studio art director Aryan Hanbeck and creative director Matt Searcy opened up about The Coalition's place in the Xbox portfolio during an interview with gaming news content creator Destin Lergarie (via MP1st ). Searcy said he and the rest of the team were "proud" when asked how they feel about Gears of War: E-Day's status as an Xbox exclusive.

"Well, we feel great because Gears has such a long, storied… It's part of Xbox's DNA. It's woven into it," he said. "At The Coalition, we feel pretty honored to have Gears and be the ones bringing that legacy forward. We know how much it means to people. We know how much it means to us."

Gears of War: E-Day is firmly a console exclusive, but there was a lot of confusion surrounding which platforms Gears of War: E-Day would be available on as recently as four months ago. The once-Xbox-exclusive franchise made its debut on PlayStation consoles when original remaster, Gears of War: Reloaded, released in August 2025. Many took its presence on PS5 as a sign not only that the series would continue to come to Sony's console but also that the days of exclusive titles may nearly be behind us – and for a while, that seemed to be the case.

Leaked listings and rumors were officially shut down at the Xbox Games Showcase 2026 when Xbox CEO Asha Sharma proudly declared that Marcus Fenix and Dom Santiago's Emergence Day prequel story would only be coming to Xbox Series X/S and PC . It was a shock decision that arrived as the Microsoft gaming entity kicked off a broader push for more exclusive games . Perhaps even more shocking at the time were the announcements that immediately followed, including the company's promise to never release Xbox exclusive titles on rival platforms .

After leaked splash art fanned rumors that Xbox hastily decided to cancel a Gears of War: E-Day PS5 port, the company said it did not make any "last-minute" decisions when it comes to its platform choice. While Searcy said it brought The Coalition joy to see their new game leading Microsoft's renewed interest in exclusive titles, making sure they made a great game was what came first.

Gears of War: E-Day Gameplay Demo Reveal Xbox Games Showcase 2026 - Screenshots

"I think this is true of most game devs: You're just passionate about your craft," he said. "We're all gamers first and foremost. We love making games. We love making Gears. So, from our perspective, we just wanted to make the best goddamn Gears game we could. We wanted it to be a technical and art showpiece, and I think getting to see Asha on-stage say, 'To return to Xbox, we're returning to Gears,' yeah, that's a really cool moment.

He continued: "We know how much Xbox means to a lot of people. We're proud to be one of Xbox's main titles – I think it's been that way for a long time – and it's pretty cool to show up now and fill that role again."

Gears of War: E-Day launched in early access for Premium Edition players on PC and Xbox Series X/S October 1, 2026. Its full launch will follow this week, October 6. IGN's early review, which covered only the campaign mode, returned a 9/10 . The game's story director was laid off just one week before it made its way to players' hands a few days ago. Now, more developers at The Coalition is bracing for additional layoffs .

articles.title: Fourth RuneScape MMO Built With Unreal Engine in the Works, Jagex Announces RuneScape Animation With MoistCr1TiKaL
articles.summary: Developer Jagex has announced a fourth MMO in the long-running RuneScape franchise, as well as an animated adaptation.
articles.body:
Developer Jagex has announced a fourth MMO in the long-running RuneScape franchise, as well as an animated adaptation.

At RuneFest in Birmingham, England, Jagex offered a glimpse at this new MMO, which it said was built “for a new generation of players.” It’s still in early development (a release isn't expected for at least a few years), and it doesn’t have an official title (Jagex is going with RS4 as a working title for now), but it will “bring the world of Gielinor to life in Unreal Engine, combining the depth, freedom and community-led spirit that have defined RuneScape for 25 years with the technology and game design possibilities of today.”

Jagex currently operates RuneScape itself, Old School RuneScape, and spinoff RuneScape: Dragonwilds. RuneScape has seen a number of major updates tied to sequel names, including a rename to RuneScape 2 in 2004 and RuneScape 3 in 2013. But both were dropped in favor of, simply, RuneScape, and it is now treated as an ongoing live service. It's tempting, then, to call this new game RuneScape 4, and it may end up justifying the name, but Jagex has yet to rubber stamp any title.

Indeed, we hardly know anything about this new RuneScape MMO, but with the mention of Unreal Engine, the expectation is it will have modern visuals and design. An image from the concept teaser and the concept teaser itself are below.

Here's the official blurb on the fourth RuneScape MMO:

Headlining RuneFest was the first glimpse of an ambitious new chapter for RuneScape: a fourth RuneScape MMO, built for a new generation of players. Still early in development, the as-yet-unnamed title will bring the world of Gielinor to life in Unreal Engine, combining the depth, freedom and community-led spirit that have defined RuneScape for 25 years with the technology and game design possibilities of today.

In a blog post , Jagex explained that it has announced RuneScape 4 so early because it wants to build on the tech development it made for Dragonwilds, and lean on the community co-development it established through RuneScape and Old School. The developer insisted RS4 is not a replacement for either RuneScape, Old School, or Dragonwilds, each of which has its own dedicated team and will continue to see investment. "We’ll be designing RS4 to sit alongside them as an additional way to experience RuneScape and the world of Gielinor," Jagex said.

"In fact, we think having different RuneScape experiences can make the whole family stronger," the developer continued. "Players may spend most of their time in one game, move between several, or discover Gielinor for the very first time through RS4. The ambition isn't to replace the RuneScape games you love. It's to make the RuneScape universe bigger."

Jagex also confirmed RS4 will be set in Gielinor, as you'd expect, and in the Sixth Age. "But we're beginning somewhere that RuneScape players have only recently started to discover - and that is Ashenfall. An area first explored in RuneScape: Dragonwilds, and a landmass to the north-east of the Gielinor.

"RS4 will take place years after the events of Dragonwilds and the destruction of the Dragon Queen Kuldra. Time has passed, the world has moved on, and Ashenfall has changed with it. But Ashenfall is only the beginning.

"Our ambition is for this adventure to grow far beyond Ashenfall over time, moving into places you know and love, as well as opening up new places and stories across Gielinor."

RuneScape is of course one of the longest-running video games in the world. Jagex says it’s seen over 300 million player accounts created in the 25 years since RuneScape first launched. But the company’s plan is to expand the franchise into new genres and even adaptations. For example, at RuneFest Jagex also announced work had started on a new RuneScape animated adaption, in partnership with YouTuber Charlie White, aka MoistCr1TiKaL, and LA-based production company Lyrical Media. Here’s the official blurb:

Additionally, Jagex unveiled plans to expand RuneScape beyond games, partnering with creator and internet phenomenon, Charlie White aka MoistCr1TiKaL as well as acclaimed LA Based production business Lyrical Media, to bring the world, characters and stories of Gielinor to life in a new exciting animated adaption.

Jagex announced a lot more at RuneFest today. Here’s everything we saw .

articles.title: Everything We Saw at RuneFest 2026, Including RuneScape 4 and RuneScape Reignited
articles.summary: RuneFest 2026 is over, and we’ve got a roundup of everything announced at Jagex’s big show celebrating its long-running fantasy MMORPG.
articles.body:
RuneFest 2026 is over, and we’ve got a roundup of everything announced at Jagex’s big show celebrating its long-running fantasy MMORPG.

This year saw a number of significant announcements, none bigger than confirmation that a fourth RuneScape MMO is in the works . Jagex hasn’t officially called it RuneScape 4 (RS4 is the working title), but we know it’s built on Unreal Engine and is designed to use the latest technology and design, so it really does sound like a next-gen RuneScape game. There’s no information on when it will be released, but the teaser trailer is below.

Jagex announced a new RuneScape animated adaptation, in partnership with YouTuber Charlie White, aka MoistCr1TiKaL, and production company Lyrical Media. No word on what this is exactly or when it will be released, but it’s happening!

Jagex announced RuneScape Reignited, which launches December 2. Jagex called it a “defining moment” for the 25-year-old game, designed to rekindle interest among lapsed players and get existing players excited. There’s a Remastered Journey and Adventure Guide, a fresh economy, and brand-new hi scores. Players can get full Reignited Access without membership from December 2-12. The long-awaited Plugin API launches this month, with players getting an early hands-on ahead of official release. The debut trailer is below:

We also got what Jagex called “the biggest roadmap in the game’s history.” 2027 content unfolds in three story arcs, all of which tie into long-running storylines. Hoard of Dragons (January) offers a sequel to the popular Dragon Slayer quest, City of Gnomes continues the gnome storyline, and Secrets of Karamja introduces a new endgame raid. Also coming is an Agility skill rework, new skilling and solo bosses, new area expansions, and a new Grandmaster Quest.

Old School RuneScape, meanwhile, got an updated roadmap. The Golden Gates to Menaphos are opening finally after 20 years, alongside a suite of fan-demanded content. The Fractured Archive, a new endgame raid, launches October 20. Hardcore Worlds launches November 4. And next year will also see the continuation of the Fairytale questline, Quest month, Dungeons of Gielinor, a Mining and Smithing rework, Chosen Commander, and the Tower of Xorphoros.

The recently released spinoff, RuneScape: Dragonwilds, saw the announcement of the Blood Crystal Saga and updated plans for 2027. The Luminance update is a prelude to 2027’s Blood Crystal Saga, and launches in December this year. This features the introduction of the Elves into RuneScape: Dragonwilds, new elven-themed customisation options for player characters and buildings alike and the Prayer skill.

The Blood Crystal Saga kicks off in 2027 starting with the Song of Rebellion in early 2027. These updates feature enemies like Moss Giants, Kebbits, and Implings, the Hunter Skill as well as new areas for players to explore, new quests and gear as well new decorations for houses inspired by the classic RuneScape city of Prifddinas.

Expect quarterly updates, which will include new Skills such as Hunter and Slayer, as well as monthly updates featuring side quests, weapons, decorations and quality of life improvements. Official modding arrives on Dragonwilds in 2027 through a new partnership with CurseForge — complete with dedicated creation tools and an in-game mod browser and installer, available across all platforms including console.

articles.title: Inde Navarrette Teases X-Men Role, Says She's 'Doing Everything Humanly Possible' to Do Rogue Justice
articles.summary: Inde Navarrette has opened up about playing Rogue in X-Men, saying she's "doing everything humanly possible" to make sure she does the character justice.
articles.body:
Inde Navarrette has opened up about playing Rogue in X-Men , saying she's "doing everything humanly possible" to make sure she does the character justice.

The Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) X-Men reboot movie has a lot to live up to. For better or worse, previous films in the mutant-centered corner of the Marvel universe spent decades establishing characters like Cyclops and Rogue, and now, Navarrette is one of a few actors set to shake everything up.

The actress, who was picked to play the power-siphoning superhero earlier this year, told the LA Times that she's not taking her role in the reboot lightly. In fact, she's doing anything but.

"I'm doing everything humanly possible because I love that character," Navarrette said. "I've studied that character. I want to do it justice for myself, for [director Jake Schrieier], for what they want to portray and also for what I as a fan want her to be like. I’m doing everything, exclamation point."

Having parts in shows like 13 Reasons Why and Superman & Lois means Navarrette has been on TV screens for years, but her role as Nikki in low-budget horror phenomenon Obsession took her fame to a new level. Through all of the Oscar buzz and turned-down parts , it was Schreier's X-Men she decided to sign on to for one of her first post-Obsession roles.

Playing Rogue in X-Men means stepping into the shoes of a character with decades of history. Aside from the Mississippi-born mutant's history in comics, she's also already appeared in numerous animated and live-action projects, with actress Anna Paquin portraying her in films like the 2000 X-Men movie and X2: X-Men United.

Meanwhile, Navarrette also recently teased some of the steps she's taking just to make sure she nails Rogue's unforgettable southern accent . While she preps for what could be the biggest role of her career, she's already got a few notable names in her corner. Last month, Lenore Zann, the voice of Rogue in multiple animated X-Men projects through the years, offered her support to the Marvel newcomer .

Navarette will take the reins – but not until 2028. The MCU X-Men Movie is currently slated to premiere May 5 of that year, and when it does, it will introduce a collection of other new actors to play familiar characters. The full list includes Navarrette as Rogue, Adam Driver as Mister Sinister, Maya Boyd as Storm, Christopher Abbott as Professor X, Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Kit Connor as Cyclops, Samara Weaving as Emma Frost, and Asa Germann as Angel . Details about its plot remain under wraps, but Schreier has teased some of the comic book stories that will inspire its story .

In the meantime, some of the previous X-Men are set to return to the big screen when Avengers: Doomsday marks the beginning of the end for another MCU saga this December. With Avengers: Secret Wars set to arrive the following year , there's no telling which other heroes will make an appearance in the near future.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Poster Highlights Doctor Doom and 3 Latverian Witches
articles.summary: Marvel Studios has revealed a new Avengers: Doomsday poster, giving audiences a closer look not only at Doctor Doom but also at the three Latverian witches who will accompany him this December.
articles.body:
Marvel Studios has revealed a new Avengers: Doomsday poster, giving audiences a closer look not only at Doctor Doom but also at the three Latverian witches who will accompany him this December.

This latest look at the new Marvel Cinematic Universe movie was shared on social media as part of this weekend's San Diego Comic-Con Málaga in Spain. It was an event that saw stars like Anthony Mackie, Winston Duke, and David Harbor make an appearance, with this latest look coming arriving as a little more than a high-res look at Robert Downey Jr.'s take on a classic comic book villain .

Doctor Doom takes center stage in the new Avengers: Doomsday poster. He's looking as menacing as ever, striking a pose similar to the one we've seen before but with somewhat better lighting. The real highlight from the new poster, however, is the three Latverian witches standing behind him.

These three witches – and their hidden identities – have been the subject of much debate amongst MCU fans the last few months. These same mystery characters brought their purple, red, and green robes to San Diego Comic-Con in California this past July. The average onlooker might assume these characters will be little more than henchmen to be discarded in a massive CGI fight sequence, but some aren't so convinced.

Warning! Potential Avengers: Doomsday spoilers follow.

Many believe the faces behind these cold metal masks may be ones we've seen before. Prominent theories suspect the witch with the red robes could be Elizabeth Olsen's Wanda Maximoff, with the green-robed witch's secret identity being Loki show alum Sophia Di Martino's Sylvie.

While not everyone has landed on the same answer for these aforementioned witches, fans are truly split when it comes to who the character wearing the purple robe is. Some say it's Kathryn Hahn's Agatha Harkness, while others believe it's Charlize Theron's Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness cameo character, Clea.

Hot Toys Avengers: Doomsday Victor von Doom Figure

As these are all just theories for now, there's always the chance all three Latverian witches could be nothing more than Doom drones for the Avengers to fight through. Still, recent developments in the MCU have led some to believe Avengers: Doomsday has some secret cameos it's saving for theaters.

Meanwhile, Mackie took his Comic-Con appearance as an opportunity to tease some of the most surprising moments from the new movie. X/Twitter user @CatherineComTH captured and shared the moment online.

"I think the big thing is the amount of doom you're going to see," he said when asked what people will be most surprised by. "Every corner we turn and every time somebody speaks, it's like, 'There's a lot of doom outside.' It's non-stop pandemonium.

"The best part about that is what the Russo brothers are great at: giving every character and every person their moment. Every time I go to watch Endgame, every single character was given their moment for the audience to connect with them and grieve with them. I think it's the same in this movie. You just have so many people."

All will be revealed when Avengers: Doomsday arrives December 18, 2026. Until then, you can see what directors Joe and Anthony Russo had to say about the film's runtime . You can also read what Nightcrawler actor Alan Cumming said regarding his lack of understanding of the movie's plot .

articles.title: Paul Sullivan: Grant Taylor and White Sox relievers keep doing ‘our little thing’ in Game 1 win
articles.summary: CLEVELAND — The last time Chicago White Sox closer Grant Taylor took the mound at Progressive Field, during a Sept. 15 showdown with the Cleveland Guardians,...
articles.body:
CLEVELAND — The last time Chicago White Sox closer Grant Taylor took the mound at Progressive Field, during a Sept. 15 showdown with the Cleveland Guardians, he watched a two-out fly ball to left field by Brayan Rocchio turn into a walk-off, two-run double in a 7-6 loss.

It was the most heartbreaking defeat of the season for the Sox and would loom large in their fall from first place in the American League Central to a wild-card spot. The Guardians won the division title and the coveted first-round bye, and the Sox were forced to go to Houston to start the postseason.

But Taylor didn't let that blown save linger, knowing he would get another chance.

And on Saturday afternoon at Progressive Field, Taylor posted a four-inning save in a 3-0 Sox win in Game 1 of the American League Division Series, giving them first blood in the best-of-five series.

After throwing three scoreless innings and 54 pitches to end Game 1 of the wild-card series, everyone was wondering what Taylor could do for an encore. How about four more scoreless frames and six strikeouts? The six K's tied for the most strikeouts in a postseason relief appearance without a walk.

"He had his stuff today" shortstop Colson Montgomery said. "He's a stud. We all knew he was the guy that was going to finish the game. We felt like it didn't matter if a guy got on or anything like that. He's our guy that you want in those late-inning situations. You can worry about (upcoming) games when you get there."

The Sox continued to out-bullpen their opponents, with five pitchers combining for the shutout, allowing only three hits with 12 strikeouts. Munetaka Murakami's two-run, 440-foot home run off Parker Messick in the fourth was all the offense the Sox needed, and Montgomery's ground-ball double to left, which had an exit velocity of 64 mph, brought home Kyle Teel from first with an insurance run in the seventh.

The Sox pitching strategy has been something to watch, even if it's not the kind of baseball you grew up watching, when aces such as Bob Gibson and Sandy Koufax finished what they started.

For the second time in three games, rookie reliever Hagen Smith was the multi-inning opener and Taylor the multi-inning closer.

Old friends, like bookends, making memories together.

Could this be the future of postseason baseball? Or is it just a Will Venable thing?

"I think in the near future it's probably a little unique," Taylor said. "Just how many times we've done it this year. … We set the record for bullpen innings this year and guys going one-plus (innings). Possibly some other teams will try to copy that, but for the most part I think it will stay relatively normal with how it's been — starting pitching goes a (few) less innings and then throw it to the guys in the middle.

The Sox bullpen's 766 innings this year were third-most in major-league history, while their 214 appearances of 1 1/3 innings or more set a major-league record. Appropriately, a photo of Jerome Holtzman, the former Chicago Tribune baseball writer who invented the save rule, hung in the Progressive Field press box. "The Dean" was no doubt smiling down on his beloved Sox, a team whose relievers rule the roost.

Taylor wasn't the only Sox pitcher who stood up when it mattered most.

Veteran Bryan Hudson, who relieved Smith in the third after the rookie walked the bases loaded, induced Chase DeLauter to fly to left to end the threat.

"That was an awesome opportunity," Hudson said. "That was probably the most adrenaline I've had in my entire life, to go out there and get one for the team."

Anthony Kay stranded the bases loaded in the fourth by getting Rocchio to fly to right, then pitched a perfect sixth to get the ball to Taylor for the end game.

The press box announcer informed the media Sean Newcomb was coming in for the bottom of the ninth, but that announcement turned out to be premature. Pitching in the shadows, Taylor struck out the side and became only the sixth reliever with a four-inning postseason save since the save became an official statistic in 1969.

"The shadows were crazy," Kay said. "His stuff is nasty already to begin with. Having those shadows put a little something extra into some of those crazy swings. He's been special all year, and for Grant to do it for four innings was even crazier."

Smith exhibited no nerves as the opener, throwing 2 2/3 scoreless innings after his three scoreless frames in Game 1 of the wild-card series. But Smith did experience control problems with three walks in the third, when his mechanics looked off, forcing Venable to call on Hudson.

"It could be that, or it could be maybe I was trying to do too much in the moment," Smith said. "I fully trust (Hudson) coming in and getting it done."

Hudson, one of their late-inning leverage relievers, said there are "no roles here" at this point of the season.

"Everyone just comes in and does their job, so we're kind of used to it," he said. "It's nothing crazy, and the guys like it, and obviously if we keep winning we love it. What we're doing is our little thing right now, but who knows what will transpire in the future?"

Kay, a starter all year, said it doesn't take much buy-in from Venable to convince the starters to be chameleons.

"I don't think he really needs to do anything," Kay said. "If you're not buying into the team's success at this point. … That's the main goal at this point — winning. I don't think anything else matters, and everyone else has bought into the idea of doing their job and handing it off to the next guy."

Hudson was credited with the win, but it was truly a group effort, the way they've operated all season. The stepping stones of the White Sox bullpen are now firmly in place for the rest of the postseason, with interchangeable parts and a collective mindset:

Baseball purists might brace their eyes at the 2026 White Sox. But the future is here, and the Sox are embracing change like no team has done before.

articles.title: How the Chicago White Sox Disarmed Cleveland’s Top Stars in Game One of the ALDS
articles.summary: Chicago White Sox have not taken their foot off the gas in this postseason. The South Side continued their surprise run, taking a 1-0 lead in their ALDS with...
articles.body:
Chicago White Sox have not taken their foot off the gas in this postseason. The South Side continued their surprise run, taking a 1-0 lead in their ALDS with a stunning 3-0 win over the Cleveland Guardians at Progressive Field on Saturday. Munetaka Murakami's two-run home run in the fourth inning off the Guardians ace Parker Messick gave the White Sox the lead. Then rookie Colson Montgomery extended it with an awkward seventh-inning RBI double, silencing any momentum the Guardians had arrived with.

However, Messick had a great start against the White Sox and looked to have stifled all of the team's offense until the fifth inning. He threw 54 pitches through the first three innings, striking out six. In that time frame, Chicago had two base runners, both in the first inning, but Messick dialed in and hammered the strike zone, reaching 98 mph. Nonetheless, the Guardians offense couldn't back up his impressive performance as the White Sox bullpen shut down the team's top players throughout the game.

Chicago White Sox Pitching Masterclass Against the Guardians

One of the major headaches for the White Sox going into the game against the Guardians was how to neutralize their small-ball identity and aggressive base running when the ball is put in play. Steven Kwan and Jose Ramirez were their top players often used to deploy the strategy, with Travis Bazzana coming along. But Hagen Smith had other ideas as he got the start and looked dominant through the first eight batters, striking out four.

‎Although Smith allowed three consecutive walks to load the bases with two outs, Bryan Hudson came on and got the final out of the third inning without any further damage. Jordan Hicks was called on by Will Venable and got two strikeouts, but walked a batter before exiting in favor of Anthony Kay . With a runner on base, Kay proceeded to give up a two-out double. He then allowed the bases to be loaded with two outs, but once again was able to get out of the jam in the bottom of the fourth inning.

Kay ended the fifth inning with no runs allowed before Grant Taylor walked to the pitcher's mound in the sixth inning. Taylor did something that rarely happens in baseball. He completed a four-inning save, giving up just two hits and striking out six batters. It was an uncommon decision from Venable to allow Taylor to pitch in more than two innings. But Taylor tossed 42 pitches aggressively, leaving no doubt.

‎Meanwhile, Kwan went 0-for-3 with a walk, failing to put a ball in play for an extra-base hit. Ramirez also went 0-for-3, and Bazzana had just one hit. The Guardians were held to just three total hits.

The White Sox will get an off-day on Sunday before facing the Guardians for Game two of the ALDS . The Sox have yet to announce the starting pitcher for Game two, but there's an expectation that it will either be Davis Martin or Sean Burke . Martin was expected to start in Game three against the Houston Astros, but the South Siders got the job done in Game two. However, should it be Martin, he would be making his postseason debut and has not pitched since September. Burke pitched four innings against the Astros.

‎The Guardians were flat on Saturday because they had six days off following the end of the regular season. So they will be seeking a bounce back on Monday. Gavin Williams will be on the mound for Cleveland, and he's known as one of the best strikeout pitchers in the American League. With a 3.76 ERA in the regular season, Williams pitched in 184 1/3 innings with 248 strikeouts. The White Sox will have to show more patience than they did against Messick to earn the second win against the Guardians in this series.

articles.title: Rasmussen has no-hit bid through 7 innings in Game 1 of Yankees-Rays AL Division Series
articles.summary: (AP) — Drew Rasmussen has a no-hit bid through seven innings, and the Tampa Bay Rays led the New York Yankees 1-0 in Game 1 of the AL Division Series on Satu...
articles.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — Drew Rasmussen has a no-hit bid through seven innings, and the Tampa Bay Rays led the New York Yankees 1-0 in Game 1 of the AL Division Series on Saturday night.

The two-time All-Star right-hander dominated a lineup that didn't include three-time AL MVP Aaron Judge, who wasn't on New York's roster because of a calf injury.

Rasmussen struck out 10 and walked two, retiring his last 13 hitters. He has thrown 64 of 94 pitches for strikes and gotten 23 swings and misses.

Rasmussen was fired up after striking out Cody Bellinger looking to end the top of the sixth. He pointed at catcher Liam Hicks, shouted a few words and smacked his fist into his glove.

He needed just 10 pitches to get through the seventh.

In his previous start against the Yankees on Sept. 22, Rasmussen pitched six hitless innings before Heliot Ramos' leadoff single in the seventh. He threw a career-high 114 pitches, helping the Rays clinch the AL East title.

Jonathan Aranda homered in the third inning off Gerrit Cole.

There have been three no-hitters in postseason history, by the Yankees' Don Larsen against the Brooklyn Dodgers in the 1956 World Series, by Philadelphia's Roy Halladay against Cincinnati in the 2010 NL Division Series and by four Houston pitchers against the Phillies in the 2022 World Series.

articles.title: Padres’ Craig Stammen gets 100% real on roof robbing home run vs. Brewers
articles.summary: The San Diego Padres suffered a 3-2 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 1 of the National League Division Series. However, a bizarre ninth-inning play invo...
articles.body:
The San Diego Padres suffered a 3-2 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 1 of the National League Division Series. However, a bizarre ninth-inning play involving Ty France quickly became the biggest talking point of the night and prompted an honest explanation from Padres manager Craig Stammen.

Following the loss, Stammen provided clarity on what happened during the unusual sequence and explained the ground rule that governs balls hitting the roof at American Family Field.

"We joked about it at the umpire meeting today about what would happen if the ball hit the roof. And it was unlikely, but it happened," Stammen said.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"The rule is if they deem the ball to be fair and it comes down, you can catch it. If it hits off the roof foul, then it's a foul ball. They ruled that it hit the roof fair, and the outfielder caught it. So unfortunately, it was a bad break for us. It looked like it was a possible home run. Just didn't go our way."

With the Padres trailing by one run in the top of the ninth inning, France appeared to hit a potential go-ahead home run with a runner on first and one out. Instead, the ball struck a cable attached to the roof at American Family Field before dropping into the glove of Brewers left fielder Jackson Chourio.

The bizarre sequence turned what initially appeared to be a potentially game-changing hit into an out, and left the Padres with very little time to respond.

San Diego challenged the ruling in an attempt to overturn the call, but the decision was ultimately upheld, allowing Milwaukee to escape with a Game 1 victory in this best-of-five playoff series .

The Padres will now attempt to put the bizarre ending behind them as they prepare for Game 2. However, France's unusual fly ball will likely remain one of the most memorable and strange moments of the 2026 MLB postseason.

articles.title: SNL Weighs in on GTA 6 vs. The Legend of Zelda With Skit Featuring Jason and Link
articles.summary: SNL weighed in on GTA 6 vs. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake with a new Weekend Update skit featuring video game protagonists Jason Duval and Link.
articles.body:
Saturday Night Live weighed in on GTA 6 vs. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake with a new Weekend Update skit featuring video game protagonists Jason Duval and Link.

Gaming fans were probably surprised to see two of November's biggest releases represented in SNL Season 52. The bit starred live-action versions of GTA 6's Jason and The Legend of Zelda's Link, played by Marcello Hernández and Mikey Day, respectively, and mostly saw the two icons arguing about who has the better game.

Also starring Weekend Update hosts Colin Jost and Michael Che, the six-minute video game skit laid it on thick with references to stealing cars, buying RPGs, and solving puzzles in the kingdom of Hyrule. You can see the SNL Weekend Update segment in question below.

The protagonists from Legend of Zelda and GTA6 stop by the Update desk pic.twitter.com/19fsg7desg — Saturday Night Live (@nbcsnl) October 4, 2026

The protagonists from Legend of Zelda and GTA6 stop by the Update desk pic.twitter.com/19fsg7desg

The SNL episode was hosted by Verity star Dakota Johnson with musical guest Turnstile and even featured a surprise cameo from pop music mega-star Taylor Swift. The long-running celebrity skit show is no stranger to nights like this, and although it's been known to feature the odd gaming reference here and there , it's safe to say full-on appearances from Link and Jason probably weren't on anyone's bingo card.

So, how did this go over with gaming fans? Well… It's not great.

"Now, I don't know much about gaming because I've had sex," Jost opened the bit, joking, "but I'm told that people are calling your releases the 'Barbenheimer of video games.'"

GTA 6 fans say Hernández's Jason leaves much to be desired, with his references to Grand Theft Auto most limited to waving around an RPG and stealing lots and lots of cars. The outfit that helped him bring Jason to life, meanwhile, is little more than a bloody bandage and a tropical button-up.

While this Jason falls more into the last-minute Halloween-costume category, Day's Link getup has received praise for being shockingly accurate to the character's specific Ocarina of Time remake tunic. It had some of the same specific details, too, and even came with elf ears and a convincing-enough wig. The jokes, however, didn't land quite as well, and mostly involved Link yelling about puzzles and arguing that his tunic is not a dress.

"I'm somebody who still watches SNL most weeks but this sketch was pretty rough," one fan online said . "Basically all of the jokes here were ones I've already been hearing for like 20 years."

"Aren't these the same jokes we've heard about Zelda since 2000?" another added .

I was simply stunned by this: how unending it was, that old ass “people who play video games never have been laid” joke, a complete disregard for specificity in service of surface level nonsense, the middle school talent show presentation. Utterly baffling. — That Week In SNL (@ThatWeekInSNL) October 4, 2026

I was simply stunned by this: how unending it was, that old ass “people who play video games never have been laid” joke, a complete disregard for specificity in service of surface level nonsense, the middle school talent show presentation. Utterly baffling.

They were trying SO hard to make Link and Zelda look like nerd shit, but you could tell the sketch fell apart at the start when the crowd cheered louder for Zelda and the puzzle joke😭 — An Average Gamer - N (@AnAverageGamerX) October 4, 2026

They were trying SO hard to make Link and Zelda look like nerd shit, but you could tell the sketch fell apart at the start when the crowd cheered louder for Zelda and the puzzle joke😭

"This is funny but also confused how they are doing a parody of a character who we don’t know that well yet," one of the more positive comments said .

The SNL skit stemmed from a place that gaming fans have been anticipating for months. Games big and small have (mostly) completely cleared out of November 2026 to avoid launching against GTA 6, with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake remaining as the biggest exception to that rule. Considering the former won't be available on the console the latter is exclusive to, there won't be quite as much competition, but gamers will absolutely still have some tough calls to make in just a little more than 30 days.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches for Nintendo Switch 2 November 5, and GTA 6 is set to follow for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19. For more, you can check out our newest look at at the new Zelda re-imagining , and you can read up on what a new age rating told us about Rockstar Games' latest .

articles.title: Avengers: Endgame Beats Avatar to Become the Highest-Grossing Movie of All Time (Again)
articles.summary: Marvel Studios' Encore re-release has helped Avengers: Endgame beat Avatar to become the highest-grossing movie at the box office of all time…again.
articles.body:
Marvel Studios' Encore re-release has helped Avengers: Endgame beat Avatar to become the highest-grossing movie at the box office of all time…again.

Despite not cracking the top five earners for this weekend's box office returns, Avengers: Endgame Encore managed to scrounge together enough cash to reach a total of $2.9255 billion worldwide. It's a number that essentially puts it just a few bucks over Avatar's standing total of $2.9237 billion, securing the Marvel movie's place as the movie to make the most in theaters.

Considering the Infinity Saga-ending team-up movie first premiered in 2019, you can probably guess that re-releases did a lot of the lifting to help it reach the number it has today. Endgame first passed Avatar when it passed $2.79 billion back in July 2019, just a few months after its initial release date. It was a milestone even director James Cameron celebrated at the time, but Marvel didn't wear the crown for long.

Thank you for assembling to make Avengers: Endgame the biggest movie of all time. We love you 3000. — Marvel Studios (@MarvelStudios) October 4, 2026

Thank you for assembling to make Avengers: Endgame the biggest movie of all time. We love you 3000.

An Avatar re-release from 2021 saw Cameron's sci-fi epic reclaim victory when its total reached more than $2.81 billion . With one re-release already under its belt , it's last weekend's Encore – which attracted a staggering $86 million in its debut – that helped it take the top spot again.

It wasn't all wins for heroes like Tony Stark and Steve Rogers, though. Endgame's new place amongst the rankings marks a narrow victory and landed it in seventh place at the domestic box office for the weekend. It also only brought in a dismal worldwide total of just $18.8 million, marking a steep decline from last weekend's numbers.

It's still an overall victory, nonetheless. With its spot so loosely secured, though, one can't help but wonder how long it will be before Avatar makes its own surprise return to theaters to take the crown once again.

Part of the allure for Avengers: Endgame Encore is the new footage it brought to the table. Although bonus content totals about four minutes of runtime across four new scenes , each segment serves as a teaser for December's Avengers: Doomsday .

The Doctor Doom introduction movie is poised to be another gigantic release for the Marvel Cinematic Universe, as it packs in even more cameos and surprises . A new poster for the film was released just yesterday.

Avengers: Endgame Encore's box office returns are seemingly crawling to a halt, so it's unclear if it will manage to hit that mythical $3 billion number despite being so painfully close to it. While we wait to see if Disney and Marvel can make it happen, you can see why some Encore watchers were disappointed to learn they were locked out of seeing all of the new teasers .

articles.title: Tom Cruise's Digger Bombs Hard With $20 Million Global Opening in Theaters
articles.summary: Tom Cruise's Digger bombed hard in theaters, pulling in an estimated $20 million in its opening weekend at the global box office.
articles.body:
Tom Cruise's Digger bombed hard in theaters, pulling in an estimated $20 million in its opening weekend at the global box office.

It's a crushing start for the Alejandro González Iñárritu-directed dark comedy. The movie, which stars an unrecognizable Cruise under a thick bed of makeup, accumulated just $8 million domestically and $12 million internationally.

It's a $20 million total that props Digger up to be crushed under the weight of its $160 million production budget (via Deadline ). With marketing costs unclear, it signals a long, long line to walk if the movie wants to even sniff at turning a profit.

"An oil tycoon faces a mounting environmental catastrophe as politicians and scientists struggle to contain the crisis," a description for Digger says. The film also stars Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, Sandra Hüller, Emma D'Arcy, and Jesse Plemons.

Digger has remained an eye-catching theatrical release for cinephiles but seems to have failed to attract the average audience member in its early October release. Reviews haven't helped, either, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting a low average for critics at 51% favorability.

Moviegoers have been infamously split on the film, with some calling it one of the worst of the year while others hope to see Cruise in the conversation for best actor. It's something the film has attempted to work in its favor , though, at least so far, it's seemingly had little impact. IGN gave it a 6/10 review , saying, "Digger's satire may not change your thinking on global warming, but there are excellent performances and more than a few laughs."

2/3 — Tom Cruise (@TomCruise) October 3, 2026

"DIGGER is officially in theaters and I am so honored to have had the opportunity to create this film alongside such talented artists," Cruise said in an X/Twitter post as totals rolled in October 3. "Thank you to the entire cast and crew for your dedication, hard work, and joy. The experience was truly unforgettable and I’m so proud of what we created."

Cruise's name was unable to stack up against the competition at the domestic box office, with Digger placed in fifth. In first by a mile was Dakota Johnson, Anne Hathaway, and Josh Hartnett's Verity , which pulled $32.6 million domestically and $30 million internationally for a worldwide total of $62.6 million. An adaptation of Colleen Hoover's novel of the same name, its story follows Johnson's Lowen Ashleigh, an author who is asked to pick up the pen for another writer after a terrible accident.

It's a mystery narrative with plenty of twists, turns, and noteworthy cast members, and it was more than enough to convince audiences to show up and see how director Michael Showalter adapted a BookTok classic for the big screen. Despite carrying similar Rotten Tomatoes scores (IGN gave it a 3/10 ), Verity found success where Digger failed.

Other domestic box office highlights include Zach Cregger's Resident Evil in second, the Brad Pitt-led Heart of the Beast in third, and Robert Pattinson's Primetime in fourth. Although Avengers: Endgame Encore , a Marvel movie re-release decorated with a few extra scenes, saw a steep decline after its big return to theaters last weekend , Marvel still managed to walk away with its own victory. Endgame, which originally released in 2019, again boasts the title of highest-grossing theatrical release of all time – for now.

Digger has a lot of shoveling to do if it wants to dig itself out of the hole it's starting off in. While we wait to see how it fares, you can check out some of IGN's top-rated movies for 2026 .

articles.title: San Diego has heartbreaking loss in NLDS series opener
articles.summary: FriarWatch: NLDS Game 2 Edition
articles.body:
What a heartbreaking way to lose a game. The San Diego Padres had what appeared to be the go-ahead run over the Milwaukee Brewers when Ty France slugged a moonshot out to left field in the top of the ninth inning. Instead, the ball hit the roof and fell straight down into Jackson Chourio's glove for an out. It almost certainly would have been a homer, but the official ruling is out.

However, San Diego had plenty of positives. The offense got to ace Jacob Misiorowski, tagging him for two runs before he was lifted in the fourth inning. After that, it got hazy. The Padres kept taking worse and worse at-bats as the game went on. Fernando Tatis Jr. and Manny Machado both struck out on three pitches in key situations. They'll need to do better to even the series this afternoon.

Logan Henderson (MIL) v. Michael King (SD)

What Henderson doesn't have in tenure, he makes up for in immense recent success. The right-hander posted a 2.47 ERA in 18 starts (98.1 IP) this season with a 1.93 ERA in his final seven starts of the year. Henderson would have been the best pitcher in Milwaukee's starting rotation if not for a young flamethrower named Jacob Misiorowski.

The 24-year old has never faced the Padres, which should be an advantage for him. His four-seamer, changeup combo is devastating, but if San Diego can have some plate discipline they should be able to beat Henderson. If their offense keeps trying to play the hero, it'll be another story.

King will be making his second start of this postseason, after pitching a gem against the Chicago Cubs in Game 1 of the Wild Card series. King took a no-hitter into the seventh that night and was incredibly dominant against a potent offense. He'll need to do the same this afternoon to give the Padres a shot at winning the series at home.

The Padres' ace faced the Brewers only once this season (May 13), when he faced off against Misiorowski. King twirled 5 2/3 innings of one-run ball. There's an immense amount of pressure on King to perform similar to his Wild Card start. If he can get through six quality innings, it'll be a huge sigh of relief for San Diego.

It was a rough game for the offense. The Padres could have won the game if they hadn't regressed so much from how they looked in the Wild Card. San Diego's lineup left 12 runners on and went a dismal 1-for-9 with runners in scoring position. The Friars will need to wake up if they have any hope of evening the Division Series in Milwaukee.

It's possible that Sheets continues to only be used in pinch-hit situations. He is still dealing with a foot injury that sidelined him for much of the stretch run. However, with his potent bat left on the bench in Game 1, it's likely that San Diego turns to the slugger in such an important moment.

The Padres expended a lot of high-leverage relievers in the series opener last night. After starter Robbie Ray went just 2 2/3 innings, San Diego turned to Bradgley Rodriguez, Yuki Matsui, Jason Adam and Adrian Morejon to pitch the final frames. Mason Miller is the only traditional reliever left for the Friars.

That being said, with the off day on Monday, it's highly likely that everyone except Morejon will be on the table. The southpaw threw two innings and probably won't pitch unless it's absolutely necessary. Matsui and Adam each threw just 15 and 16 pitches, respectively, so they'll factor as the first out of the 'pen. Should King stumble early, Randy Vásquez could enter the game in bulk relief.

articles.title: White Sox stick with bullpen plan: Anthony Kay to open AL Division Series Game 2 vs. Guardians
articles.summary: CLEVELAND (AP) — Will Venable said before the start of the American League Division Series that it was possible the Chicago White Sox could use bullpen games...
articles.body:
CLEVELAND (AP) — Will Venable said before the start of the American League Division Series that it was possible the Chicago White Sox could use bullpen games during the first three contests against the Cleveland Guardians.

Venable isn't deviating from that plan, so far.

Anthony Kay will be the opener for Game 2 on Monday at Progressive Field. It will be the 33rd time this season the White Sox have used an opener, including the third in the postseason.

Sean Burke is expected to throw most of the innings, but Venable said he will have many options available.

"The way it's set up here with the two off days in between these first three games gives us a chance to go ahead," Venable said.

Kay made 33 appearances during the regular season, including 31 starts, and went 10-9 with a 4.44 ERA. He was the first White Sox left hander to earn double-digit wins in a season since Carlos Rodón with 13 in 2021. Kay got the win on Wednesday in Game 2 of the Wild Card Series with two-thirds of a scoreless inning.

Kay was also among five Chicago pitchers in Saturday's 3-0 victory as they allowed only three hits and struck out 12.. He went 1 1/3 innings and allowed one hit and one walk.

"It's been interesting watching him in a different type of role, shorten down. You've seen the velo tick up. I think the one thing is he just hasn't been afforded kind of that length to get comfortable," Venable said. "He's made some really big pitches, got us out of some really tough spots. We just haven't really seen us go beyond that."

Chicago's bullpen has a 4.57 ERA with its openers, but Hagen Smith has not allowed an earned run in 5 2/3 innings in the postseason. The left-hander worked three scoreless innings in Game 1 of the first round against Houston and then 2 2/3 shutout innings on Saturday against the Guardians.

Burke got the start on Wednesday in Houston. The right-hander, who went 11-7 with a 3.34 ERA in the regular season, allowed three runs on four hits and struck out eight in four innings.

"I think just seeing the efforts and everybody kind of doing their own individual role just makes you want to take the ball and just do anything you can to kind of help the team just put up zeros, and passing that baton to the next guy," Burke said. "And the way we're doing this is really just like a team effort from the pitching side."

Gavin Williams will get the call for Cleveland. The right-hander went 14-8 with a 3.76 ERA and was second in the major leagues with 248 strikeouts. He held opposing hitters to a .213 batting average, tied for seventh best in the majors.

Williams isn't stressing about the start despite the Guardians needing a win to avoid an 0-2 deficit going to Chicago.

"It's just another game. Just going to go out there and try and do what I know I can do and execute and try to help the team win," he said.

articles.title: James Gunn Shuts Down Jensen Ackles Batman Casting Rumors
articles.summary: DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn has shut down rumors that Supernatural star Jensen Ackles has been cast as the DCU's Batman.
articles.body:
DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn has shut down rumors that Supernatural star Jensen Ackles has been cast as the DCU's Batman.

Social media feeds caught fire over the weekend when comic book fans learned that The Boys alum had recently followed the DC movie bigwig on Instagram. Ackles, a self-proclaimed Batman fanatic, has long been a fan-favorite pick to play Bruce Wayne in the DCU, but if he is joining the budding cinematic superhero universe, he hasn't done it quite yet.

Gunn poured cold water on the recently reignited rumors over on his preferred social media platform, Threads, when replying to a post covering the subject earlier today. He said he had no idea Ackles had dropped him a follow and that he was "going to follow him back." Sadly, that's about the extent of their interactions over the years.

"Thanks for letting me know," Gunn said. "I'm going to follow him back. I met him once 20 years ago when he was dating a friend of mine. Nice guy. We haven't cast him as anything yet."

While the "yet" in that sentence might give some hope, any dreams that the actor might play Batman have been put to rest, at least for now. Fans have long named Ackles as their pick to play the Caped Crusader in some form for a few reasons, including the fact that he already doesn't look half bad wearing the Batsuit.

The Dean Winchester actor has famously suited up in full Batman gear before and even made IGN's list for best celebrity Halloween outfits in 2019 . He wears the cowl well, but he's proven to have the gruff vocals required for the part, too.

@TheBoysOOCC Batman ? — Billy Iskandar (@billyiskandar05) October 3, 2026

Ackles is a DC regular who has played Batman in animated projects like Batman: The Long Halloween, Legion of Super-Heroes, Justice League: Warworld, and Justice League: Crisis on Infinite Earths. He also showed up in Batman: Under the Red Hood as former Robin Jason Todd. In other words, even if Ackles isn't the DCU's Batman, he's certainly laid the groundwork for the jump to live-action crimefighting to make enough sense.

Alas, Gunn's cinematic universe remains without a Dark Knight to keep Gotham safe. So far, we've only received the occasional reference to a DCU Batman as projects like 2025's Superman and Lanterns plant the seeds for a proper introduction. While audiences will finally dive headfirst into a new Gotham City when Clayface tells the horrific tale of its titular villain later this month, it seems we'll have to wait until the long-in-development The Brave and the Bold for a proper introduction to Batman .

In the meantime, Robert Pattinson is still set to reprise his role as an Elseworlds Bruce Wayne when The Batman Part 2 premieres next year. Additionally, Gunn and fellow co-CEO Peter Safran will reportedly remain in charge of the DCU for the foreseeable future despite the big changes going on at Warner Bros. and Paramount . Lanterns will put a cap on its explosive first season in just a few hours, with Superman follow-up, Man of Tomorrow , still expected to premiere in Julym 2027.

articles.title: Blade Director Defends 'Good Dude' Kevin Feige After Marvel Scrapped Mahershala Ali's 1920s Vampire Movie
articles.summary: Blade director Bassam Tariq said he felt like a "failure" after exiting the Mahershala Ali-led Marvel movie, but he doesn't blame MCU mastermind Kevin Feige for how things went down.
articles.body:
Blade director Bassam Tariq said he felt like a "failure" after exiting the Mahershala Ali-led Marvel movie, but he doesn't blame MCU mastermind Kevin Feige for how things went down.

The filmmaker, who was the first of two directors officially tied to Marvel Studios' now-canceled 1920s vampire movie, offered his honest thoughts about the project and even shared some new details about its story during an interview with Vulture . With a resume that includes films like 2012 documentary These Birds Walk, 2020's Mogul Mowgli, and last month's Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, it seemed Blade is the movie that hit Tariq the hardest.

"I didn't know which way north was," he said of his Blade exit . "Afterward, I had to kind of disconnect from everybody. I don't know if that was the right thing to do, but it was one of those things where I had to find myself again. When you're doing it at that level, and it doesn't work out, you're like, 'S**t, I feel like a failure, because I couldn't do the thing that I wanted to do well.' You're trying to recalibrate who you are.

"My wife, my children, and the Atlanta Muslim community really were there for me. They helped me reground myself and understand what it is that I really care about. They all knew me as the guy that's directing Blade. And it was like, 'Oh, he left? Snap, OK.' I was afraid they would always be asking about this or that, but nobody ever talked about it. We just moved on, and they didn't really care, and it was so great to be around people that just didn't give a s**t."

Tariq had a tough time, partially, he said, because the ideas he had for Blade were so cool. Although his involvement came to an end because "they wouldn't let me write the script, and life's too short to make really disastrous things," the director teased that the now-abandoned sets they had in New Orleans were "incredibly designed" and "beautiful."

He said the 1920s vampire movie was going to have "an incredible horse chase through" these sets that started "in a speakeasy where Blade would act drunk." The problem was the Marvel crew "didn't have all the pieces to really get it together, to be what it needed to be." Tariq recalled the work of production designer Stefania Cella and her team as one of the most heartbreaking parts of the film's cancellation.

"That's the part that breaks my heart the most, all of the craftsmen and craftswomen that were working on the thing," he explained. "But all that energy also needs to be put into good words on the page, and that's not a hit on any of the writers. The writers were working really hard. It was just – I think Kevin can admit it, too – he had a lot on his plate.

Marvel announced its Marvel Cinematic Universe reboot with Ali as its star all the way back in 2019, but as updates rolled in through the years , it only became more apparent that it would never come to be. It was finally, officially canceled in July of this year.

Feige has caught a lot of flak – some even self-inflicted – in the aftermath of Blade's cancellation. He called himself a "gigantic loser and failure" over its failure to launch just weeks before it was finally killed, with Ali going on to agree with Feige's assessment of himself . It's been painful to watch unfold, but Tariq doesn't hold the MCU orchestrator responsible for how everything went down.

The ex-Blade director spent chunk of his new interview calling the Marvel movie producer "adaptable," explaining that he "listens and f**king changes." Using Spider-Man: Brand New Day as an example, he said it's clear that Marvel Studios listens and makes shifts to make sure viewers "still got spectacle" while "building with story along the way."

Tariq called the wide web that is the MCU Feige's world, "and rightfully so."

"He's done such incredible films, and he's made massive amounts of money for Disney," he said. "Of course they're going to trust him over me, who had made just one film. I made a film. I made Mogul Mowgli with a budget of $1.2 million, and we built this massive set that was the equivalent of like, 10 Mogul Mowglis. So, of course, the last word should go to Kevin. It makes perfect sense. We just never really had a script."

Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother is out now and just so happens to star Ali as the lead. Blade may never step out of the shadows in the MCU, but the actor said he's still thankful for the free year of training it gave him for his new movie . As far as Tariq is concerned, he's hoping Feige finds time to see what he's capable of as a filmmaker.

"I want to be clear: I like Kevin," he added. "I'd love to talk to him if he sees it. He's a good dude. I really dislike all this s**t about like, 'Marvel fumbled this. F**k Kevin Feige.' No, man. He's got a lot on his plate, too much. And I think we also had this impossible task of trying to compete with the first superhero movie, which is Wesley Snipes' iconic Blade . It's really such a massive undertaking in a way that affected so many people."

articles.title: Brewers 3B coach jokingly predicted a ball off the roof in pre-Game 1 meeting
articles.summary: OF COURSE it happened after that.
articles.body:
Brewers third base coach Matt Erickson has seen his share of games at American Family Field since joining the Milwaukee coaching staff in 2022. And like everyone else who watched Saturday's Game 1 of the NLDS, he had never seen a baseball hit the stadium's roof in fair territory.

So, of course Erickson predicted that astonishing ordeal before Game 1.

With the Padres down a run in the ninth inning, Ty France thought he gave San Diego the lead when his 105.3 mph fly ball left his bat. But the ball ended up deflecting off the roof over fair territory and fell squarely into Jackson Chourio's glove for the out.

Though there was confusion throughout the stadium in the moment, the very scenario was discussed in the ground rules meeting with the umpires before the game. That was where Erickson jokingly predicted the fluky play.

Erickson said, "Haven't seen it here in six years, so it will happen tonight."

Baseball has a funny habit of working things out that way.

articles.title: Walt Weiss Must Stop Saving Chris Sale For The Eighth
articles.summary: The Braves wasted their best arms in Game 1. Walt Weiss saved the tank too early. Chris Sale needs to start Game 2 or the season ends.
articles.body:
Walt Weiss made a massive error by holding back his best arms in the NLDS. The manager saved premium options for a game where the team already trailed. This approach ignores the reality that October baseball demands immediate action. Saving your ace for late innings when you are behind makes no sense.

According to Battery Power , the sole justification for today's action is that Chris Sale cannot pitch Game 2. If Sale is healthy, using him later is "absolutely infuriating and completely unnecessary." Weiss told reporters that "today was going to be tough for us to chase from behind because of how we emptied the tank on Thursday night." That explanation falls flat when you see Brent Suter pitching the seventh and eighth innings.

Braves fans have seen this pattern before. The idea of "punting" a game works in May or June to save strength for the long season. But this is October. The stakes are too high to use your 12th or 13th best pitcher in a tight game. Battery Power points out that the team should have used Dylan Dodd or AJ Smith-Shawver for short stints. Instead, they relied on veterans who might not have the energy left. This is a cost of doing business that the team cannot afford right now.

The writer loves Victor Mederos and thinks he has been a revelation. Yet the team scrimp and save for seven months just to get to the postseason. Once there, they should spend their options lavishly. The best players must perform when the lights are brightest. Holding back Chris Sale to possibly have him enter the eighth inning tomorrow is a waste of talent.

Walt Weiss claims he is not worried about having enough pitching. He stated, "Look, you've got Sale and Mahle still. Tomorrow a much more rested bullpen. Yeah, I don't have any worries about … having enough pitching. We've got plenty of pitching." This confidence ignores the current situation. If Sale is available for Game 2, he should start. The manager cannot let the game slip away because he is saving his top arm.

AJ Smith-Shawver should not lose heart. Right now, he must be prepared to strike out three batters. He could break into the starting rotation in 2027. But tonight is not the night to test the limits of the bullpen. The team needs its best options to win now. Battery Power argues that if the game is close, the manager must upshift. Downshifting when you are down is a recipe for failure.

The Braves have decided not to use Chris Sale in Game 2; Ray Kerr will start Sunday, with Sales lined up for Game 3 on Tuesdday. Weiss cannot claim the day was tough to chase from behind while still holding back his ace. The fans want to see the best team on the field. Saving your strength for a game you might not win is a bad strategy. The season is over if they do not adjust.

articles.title: Blindfolded Tekken 8 Player Achieves One of the Game’s Top Ranks from Beginner
articles.summary: Professional Tekken 8 player SuperBrine is going viral after reaching God of Destruction using Alisa while completely blindfolded with a sleep mask.
articles.body:
Professional Tekken 8 player SuperBrine is going viral after reaching God of Destruction using Alisa while completely blindfolded with a sleep mask.

SuperBrine has been streaming his run on Twitch in the form of seven separate broadcasts, starting in June 2026 . The final stream from this series, broadcast in early October , has become a hot topic within the fighting game community, as he was able to reach one of the game’s top ranks from Beginner while obscuring his vision with a sleep mask.

It’s an impressive feat no matter how you swing it, standing as a testament to SuperBrine’s skill as a player and Tekken 8’s laudable sound design — but, perhaps unsurprisingly, his blindfolded run from Beginner to God of Destruction has sparked no end of debate about the game's difficulty and Alisa’s ease of use as a character.

HERE WE ARE... First person ever to get From BEGINNER to GoD rank 100% Blindfolded on LIVE stream This took me alot of effort and time, but hell yea worth it. my whole run from the beginning to the end is SAVED in my twitch highlights. a new youtube video incoming #TEKKEN8 — SuperBrine (@SuperBrineTK) October 4, 2026

HERE WE ARE... First person ever to get From BEGINNER to GoD rank 100% Blindfolded on LIVE stream This took me alot of effort and time, but hell yea worth it. my whole run from the beginning to the end is SAVED in my twitch highlights. a new youtube video incoming #TEKKEN8

I got the chance to sit down with SuperBrine to discuss his self-imposed challenge and find out if it was legit or not. He confirmed that there was no way he was able to see through the sleep mask (which are typically made out of thick material with dense cushions on the eyes), and reiterated that he’d streamed his entire run live on Twitch for all to see, so there was no way for him to cheat.

As for the ‘why’ of it all, SuperBrine said he wanted to prove that he could do something impossible, and is hopeful the challenge will help boost his visibility as a pro player. He also admitted that this undertaking was not, in any way, meant as a criticism of Tekken 8 as a game, despite the discourse surrounding his efforts on social media.

“My primary goal was simply to take on a challenge that most people will consider impossible and prove that I can do it,” he said. “I want to clarify that I didn't do this to criticize the game or suggest that it's poorly designed in any way. It's actually the exact opposite. I genuinely love this game, and I thrive on pushing my own personal limits through these kinds of extreme challenges. I am deeply passionate about it, and since my long-term plan is to pursue competing as my professional career, these kinds of challenges will directly support my career."

Outside of being unable to see, SuperBrine revealed that the hardest part of this challenge was that his eyes began to burn from being closed so long beneath the sleep mask. This, on top of being mentally drained from putting so much effort into the task, forced him to take frequent breaks.

“The physical toll was actually surprising. …Mentally, it required extreme patience, without it, completing this run simply wouldn't be possible,” he said.

Even a top player would have difficulty on ranked if blindfolded, so how did SuperBrine manage to pull it off? He told me that he relied on his foundational skills as a fighting game player and a keen sense of how people play on different ranks, as well as Tekken 8's helpful sound cues.

“It comes down to a massive amount of foundational experience. Playing on multiple smurf accounts over time gave me an exact read on the game knowledge players have at different ranks. Because of that, I knew precisely which strings and flowcharts would work and which wouldn't. Beyond that, precise hearing is crucial. You would be able to instantly differentiate specific sounds knowing whether a move resulted in a wall splat or not, if it was a hit or a block, and if you landed a counter hit versus a normal hit. Ultimately, it’s all about paying attention to the audio and knowing exactly the type of player you are facing," he explained.

For those who believe that Tekken 8 is so easy that anyone can pick up a blindfold and a controller and get to God of Destruction, SuperBrine invites you to try it; but it’s not that simple, because if it was, anyone would be able to do it.

“People are free to have their own opinions on it. There will always be positive and negative ones, and I respect that. But turning this into a criticism of Tekken 8 will not help the future of the game. You can't reach God of Destruction blindfolded just by picking a specific character and hoping for the best. It takes thousands of hours of game knowledge, knowing what kind of players you will face and what level of game knowledge they have, and relying entirely on audio cues. If it was just a flaw in the game or an easy character, someone else would have done it already,” he said.

SuperBrine chose to give himself this challenge; there are many other fighting game players who have reached top ranks and even become pros in spite of having actual disabilities. For instance, the late great BrolyLegs was a top Street Fighter player who could duke it out with the best of them using only his mouth to move his controller. And BlindWarriorSven, a blind Street Fighter 6 player who lost his eyesight at six years old due to cancer, won a livestreamed set at Evo 2-1 with E. Honda thanks the game’s impressive accessibility features that allowed him to 'hear' where his opponent was at on-screen.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Mighty Mike Plays Dad Says He Owns 'Like 12 Companies,' Promises Refunds for AI Shirts
articles.summary: Mighty Mike Plays dad Dave has promised refunds and issued a lengthy explanation after the internet demanded more information about the YouTube ads allegedly purchased by his son and the drama that followed.
articles.body:
Mighty Mike Plays dad Dave has promised refunds and issued a lengthy explanation after the internet demanded more information about the YouTube ads allegedly purchased by his son and the drama that followed.

The saga began when a father took to his son's YouTube channel, Mighty Mike Plays, to announce that his child had allegedly used a company credit card to purchase $118,000 in video ads. It was a painful and highly relatable story that snowballed into a full-fledged internet spectacle when pricey AI-generated T-shirts and questionable details led many online to look for concrete answers.

The controversial father figure came clean in a new video titled " Allow me to Explain " that was uploaded to the Mighty Mike Plays channel last week (via Dexerto ). Dave started the hour-long explainer – which has since been deleted and re-uploaded on a new YouTube channel called Coffee Time with Dave – promising that everyone who purchased one of those T-shirts would receive a refund.

“this might be the end of Mighty Mike Plays…” is the funniest thing you could say in front of your dad after putting him 118k in debt and getting him fired — Mako Fukasame 🦈👩‍🏫 | Vershion AU (@MakoFukasame) September 15, 2026

“this might be the end of Mighty Mike Plays…” is the funniest thing you could say in front of your dad after putting him 118k in debt and getting him fired

"Dave here. A.k.a. Devoted Dave. A.k.a. Dazzling Dave. A.k.a. Dependable Dave, and the list goes on," Dave said. "I want to give you guys an update: First off, I'm going to say that everyone that got a shirt got refunded whether they asked for it or not. So, whether you wanted a refund or not, you got it."

The full video covers allegations related to the Mighty Mike Plays drama and also covers a lot that has nothing to do with it at all. Dave's headline he wants to share, though, is that this all blew up so much faster and so much bigger than he ever expected it to be.

He explained that he thought he was simply "venting" about his son's spending with a story that sounds like the kind of thing you'd tell a friend at a bar. Millions of views and a sea of video responses later, and it's clear it didn't pan out the way he ever imagined it would.

"I remember thinking, like, you know, I wonder if this video will hit 10,000 views," he said. "That's kind of where I thought it would cap. I didn't think it would go so viral. Everything happened real-time, organically, and I obviously didn't handle everything the right way, essentially, but just to make it clear: I didn't come to YouTube to ask for help. I wasn't looking for any sort of help."

Part of the reason why the internet gathered with Minecraft fans to help out is because Dave said the $118,000 hole his son put in his company card resulted in him being fired. He also stated he had just 30 days to make up for the missing money, but in the new video, Dave has clarified some of those details.

Instead of losing his job, Dave suggested he technically was not fired in a traditional sense, with that part of the story being a "simplified version" of what actually happened. The reality, he said, is that "the contract between company A and company B just got terminated," adding, "isn't that the same thing?" As many had suspected, he doesn't just own his own company – he owns 12.

"Yeah, I own my own company. So what?" Dave clarified. "In fact, you guys didn't even see – I have like 12 companies. Not all of them are productive, as we speak. Some of them are just collecting dust, and just because someone has a company or is a CEO doesn't mean that, 'Oh, OK. Just by having those titles you're actually conducting a profitable business.'"

He continued: "But just to clarify, I consider that being fired. If my company lost a contract with this important company, then, I mean, how is that not being fired? Fine. I'll be more specific next time."

As for those controversial T-shirts and why he's issuing refunds, Dave said he "didn't want to sit around and let these actual scammers sell people who wanted to be involved in this story." His plan for an official merch page, which allegedly put him "another $10K in the hole," still drew much ire from the internet, at least partially due to its prolific use of AI-generated designs. He explained why he's issued refunds – even if not all that many people found something to buy.

"In retrospect, was AI and the merch the way to go? Was the price the way to go? No," he said. "Look, I'm going to admit when I was wrong: That was not the move. I shouldn't have used AI. Although, at the time, I know I defended it. There is a now-infamous deleted post, which I crashed out."

He later added: "I do agree now, and if I could go back, I'd do it differently, but again, I didn't have the luxury of time. Time was running out. We had to figure something out, so yeah, I had AI create some designs. I still feel like those designs were flawless, gorgeous, beautiful, superb, and there is about 100 people who got free shirts."

It's unclear if Dave's explanation video will be enough to satisfy the many online who looked into the Minecraft YouTube channel after the events surrounding it kicked off last month. If this is the first time you're hearing of Mighty Mike Plays and the drama surrounding AI-generated T-shirt designs, there's no need to fear. We broke down everything you could ever want to know about the story right here .
